Only this one test file exists (the only other `*AgentTest.java`), and the same 3 failures reappear — confirming they're not environment flukes.

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` with 28 JUnit 5 tests. 25 pass; 3 fail, each revealing a real bug in `ExtendedBufferedReader`:

1. **`testLineNumberForEmptyStreamIsZero`** — Reading an empty stream makes `getLineNumber()` return `1` instead of `0`. In `read()`, the EOF-triggered line-increment condition (`current == EOF && lastChar != CR && lastChar != LF && lastChar != EOF`) doesn't exclude the initial `UNDEFINED` state, so hitting EOF on a never-read stream wrongly counts a phantom line.

2. **`testBulkReadAtEofReturnsEofAndSetsLastChar`** — `getPosition()` decreases after the bulk `read(char[], int, int)` hits EOF. The code does `position += len`, and when `len == EOF (-1)`, that subtracts 1 from the position instead of leaving it unchanged (repeated EOF calls make it decrease further).

3. **`testBulkReadLineNumberConsistentWithSingleCharReadAtEof`** — For an unterminated final line (e.g. `"abc"` with no trailing newline), the bulk `read(char[], int, int)` method never increments the line counter on EOF (unlike the single-char `read()`, which does), so `getLineNumber()` incorrectly drops from `1` back to `0` once EOF is reached via the bulk-read API — inconsistent with the single-char read path on identical input.
